alt: The prefix-sum method with a running minimum. The prefix array sits under the values. A marker shows low, the smallest prefix entry seen so far, and another shows the end being tried. For each end, the best sum ending there is the end entry minus low, and the matching run of values is marked. The best sum so far is kept, and low moves whenever a smaller entry appears.

steps.caption: prefix is [0, 3, -1, 1, 0, 4, -1], built in one pass. low starts at prefix[0], which is 0, and best starts at values[0], which is 3.
j = 0: cand is prefix[1] - low = 3 - 0 = 3, the sum of values[0:1]. It does not beat best, which stays 3.
j = 1: cand is prefix[2] - low = -1 - 0 = -1, the sum of values[0:2]. It does not beat best, which stays 3.
prefix[2] is smaller than low, so low moves there and becomes -1. A run starting at values[2] would subtract this smaller entry.
j = 2: cand is prefix[3] - low = 1 - (-1) = 2, the sum of values[2:3]. It does not beat best, which stays 3.
j = 3: cand is prefix[4] - low = 0 - (-1) = 1, the sum of values[2:4]. It does not beat best, which stays 3.
j = 4: cand is prefix[5] - low = 4 - (-1) = 5, the sum of values[2:5]. It beats best, so best becomes 5.
j = 5: cand is prefix[6] - low = -1 - (-1) = 0, the sum of values[2:6]. It does not beat best, which stays 5.
Every end has been tried against the smallest prefix before it. best is 5, the largest sum of any run of consecutive values.
prefix is [0, -4, -6, -13], built in one pass. low starts at prefix[0], which is 0, and best starts at values[0], which is -4.
j = 0: cand is prefix[1] - low = -4 - 0 = -4, the sum of values[0:1]. It does not beat best, which stays -4.
prefix[1] is smaller than low, so low moves there and becomes -4. A run starting at values[1] would subtract this smaller entry.
j = 1: cand is prefix[2] - low = -6 - (-4) = -2, the sum of values[1:2]. It beats best, so best becomes -2.
prefix[2] is smaller than low, so low moves there and becomes -6. A run starting at values[2] would subtract this smaller entry.
j = 2: cand is prefix[3] - low = -13 - (-6) = -7, the sum of values[2:3]. It does not beat best, which stays -2.
prefix[3] is smaller than low, so low moves there and becomes -13. A run starting at values[3] would subtract this smaller entry.
Every end has been tried against the smallest prefix before it. best is -2, the largest sum of any run of consecutive values.
prefix is [0, 1, 3, 6, 10], built in one pass. low starts at prefix[0], which is 0, and best starts at values[0], which is 1.
j = 0: cand is prefix[1] - low = 1 - 0 = 1, the sum of values[0:1]. It does not beat best, which stays 1.
j = 1: cand is prefix[2] - low = 3 - 0 = 3, the sum of values[0:2]. It beats best, so best becomes 3.
j = 2: cand is prefix[3] - low = 6 - 0 = 6, the sum of values[0:3]. It beats best, so best becomes 6.
j = 3: cand is prefix[4] - low = 10 - 0 = 10, the sum of values[0:4]. It beats best, so best becomes 10.
Every end has been tried against the smallest prefix before it. best is 10, the largest sum of any run of consecutive values.
